title: Rook against pawn
line: The rook stops the pawn if its king gets there in time.

steps.text: Here the rook alone cannot stop the pawn, because its king walks up beside it. The rook needs its own king to arrive in time.
Bring your king toward the pawn by the shortest way. Every step counts.

steps.text: Now you have Black. Here a pawn that runs ahead of its king is lost. Walk them up together.
Bring your king beside the pawn before you push it.

steps.hint: Step to the side of the pawn, one row ahead of your king.
steps.after: The pawn is guarded, and the white king is far away. The game is drawn.

summary: A rook needs its king to stop a pawn that its own king supports. Count the steps: one is often the difference.
